Hi Sean —

Quick question as we're finalizing SOW language. Our app opens an active session (long chat) but often issues many small follow-ups (single-turn calls) that are only a few tokens. On the invoice we see a 1k-token floor being applied on a handful of those tiny calls and it's materially increasing our spend.

Can you confirm how Redwood treats the "minimum billing quantum" in these cases: is the floor applied to each API call independently, or is there an amortization/rolling context rule (e.g., attributes small calls to an active session prefix so they don't all hit the floor)?

We're trying to decide whether we need to request a billing concession or if we should change our client to batch small follow-ups. I've attached the last month's invoice excerpt for reference.

Sean/Tessa — wrote up the technical/contract language below so we have a single source of truth to send to Atlas. TL;DR: we apply amortization when calls meet prefix/KV affinity and fall within the active session window; otherwise the per-call floor applies.

Billing heuristics (current prod behavior):
- Session affinity: a call is eligible for rolling-context amortization if it references a session ID or reuses the same KV cache/prefix token fingerprint within a 30-minute active window.
- Prefix attribution: tokens consumed by the prefix (initial prompt + persistent system context) are amortized across eligible subsequent calls; each eligible call is charged only for delta tokens unless it triggers a new model context load.
- Minimum quantum/rounding: we bill in 100-token quanta with a 1,000-token invoice floor applied per independent "charging bucket." For amortized calls, the bucket is the active session; for stateless calls the bucket is the single request. Rounding to the nearest quantum occurs at the bucket level.

Concrete examples (simplified):
- Example A (stateless batch): three independent short calls (10 tokens each) not tied to a session => three buckets, each rounded to 100 tokens => billed 300 tokens (hit floor if account minimum applies).
- Example B (session amortized): long chat creates a session with 800 tokens prefix. Over the next 24 hours Atlas issues 50 small follow-ups (5 tokens each) that reuse the session ID and KV cache. Those follow-ups are attributed to the session bucket: they add 250 tokens total (50 * 5) and the entire session bucket is rounded to quanta and subject to the 1,000-token floor only once. Net effect: amortized vs per-call billing reduces surface area dramatically.

Edge cases and notes:
- Session expiry: any call that rehydrates the entire model (no KV reuse) is considered a fresh bucket.
- Time window: the 30-minute active window is conservative; we can extend it by configuration for Dedicated/Private deployments if Atlas needs it documented.
- Pilot measurement: we can produce per-call attribution logs (CSV) so Atlas can independently verify which calls were amortized vs billed independently.

Suggested contract clause (short):
"For the purposes of metering, Redwood will amortize token usage across calls that reuse an active session identifier and KV cache within a 30-minute active window. Independent stateless calls are billed per-call. Token usage is rounded to 100-token quanta at the bucket level."

Happy to revise language if legal/product want different phrasing.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Billing & Product Finance Lead, Redwood Inference
